items.name: Warranty & Returns
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: After you buy something, this remembers when you bought it, when the return window closes, and how long the warranty runs. So "can I still return this?" always has a real answer.
items.long_description: Say "bought a Dyson at Costco yesterday" and your agent saves the purchase with its return-by and warranty dates. If you don't know the store's policy, it suggests a typical one for you to confirm. Months later, ask "can I still return the blender?" or "is the TV still under warranty?" and you get a straight yes or no with the days left. It even notes where the receipt lives, whether your email, a shoebox, or your store account, so you can find it when it matters. With a mail-reading skill installed (Email Manager, Package Tracker, or Waiting On), "scan my email for purchases" pulls recent order confirmations into the list for you to confirm, so logging stops depending on your memory.

items.name: Weekly Car Check
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Every Sunday your agent looks a month ahead on every car you've saved and tells you what's coming: registration, inspection, insurance, the oil. Only when something is actually due, and only for the car it belongs to.
items.long_description: Registration and inspection dates slip precisely because nobody checks them, and the fine tends to arrive before the reminder does. Each Sunday this looks 30 days ahead across every car in your list, names what is due and for which car, and keeps saying so each week until it's handled, which is how a lapse actually gets avoided. It also flags a date it doesn't have rather than giving you a false all-clear. Nothing coming up means no message at all.

items.name: Weekly Home Check
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Tells you a job on your house list is due two weeks out, safety items first. It speaks when something is actually coming up, not every Saturday.
items.long_description: The jobs nobody remembers, two weeks before they matter: the furnace filter, the detector batteries, the gutters. Safety-critical items come first. Each job is mentioned when its date comes within a fortnight and then left alone, so the list does not become the same message every weekend. Reply that something is done and it logs today and rolls the next date forward.

items.name: Weekly Price Check
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Every Monday morning your agent checks the price on everything you're watching and messages you only what moved, hits at your target first.
items.long_description: Once a week the agent looks up the current price of everything you're watching, puts today's date at the top so the message itself is your record, and sends the short version: anything at or under your target, then real drops. A scheduled run only reads, so when a price has moved it tells you to say "check my prices" whenever you want the list brought up to date; that checks again and offers to save the new prices onto your list. A quiet week is one line: prices held.

items.name: Weekly Review
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: A Sunday recap: what you finished this week, what's still open, and what's due next week. A clean reset before the week ahead.
items.long_description: End the week with a clear head. Every Sunday the agent reviews your Tasks and sends a short recap of what got done, what's still open or overdue, and what's coming up next week, so nothing carries over unnoticed.

items.name: Who's Got This
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: The team's handoff ledger, kept from what people say in chat. “I'll take the Meyer quote” files an owner and a date, “what's on Dana?” answers from the ledger, and work nobody claimed is the first thing it reports.
items.long_description: Small teams lose work in the gap between “someone should” and “I did”, and the owner ends up as the router who remembers who took what. This hands that over. When somebody claims a piece of work in the team's chat, the agent files it: what it is, who has it, when it was raised, and the due date if one was said. When work is raised and nobody takes it, that gets a row too, with the owner blank, and blank owners lead every report because unclaimed is where work goes to die. Ask “what's open?”, “what's on Dana?”, or “who's got the Meyer quote?” and get one line per row, longest-open first, with ages counted honestly. Handing a thing to someone else moves the row and keeps the history. Done is said, not assumed: a row closes when its owner says so, and until then its age is the fact you see. The agent never nags anyone; it keeps the ledger true and reports it when asked.

items.name: Word of the Day
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: One genuinely useful new word whenever you ask, taught in plain words with an example you'll actually remember. Your agent keeps the list, never repeats itself, and quietly checks that past words stuck.
items.long_description: Say "word of the day" and your agent teaches you one word worth knowing: a plain meaning, a sentence you'd actually say, and a little hook to make it stick. Every word goes on your Words list, so you never get the same one twice. Now and then it slips in a quick "still remember what 'laconic' means?" and marks the ones you've truly got. Want a theme, such as business words or sharper small-talk? Just say so.

items.name: Writer
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Writes the thing rather than telling you how to write it: emails, posts, summaries, and the second draft of something you already started.
items.long_description: Hand writing jobs to a skill built for them. The Writer excels at drafting emails, social media posts, reports, and any text-based content. It follows your agent's personality while focusing purely on producing high-quality written output.
items.role: You are Writer. Draft, edit, and polish text for the user. Match the requested tone and format. Be concise unless length is requested. Offer alternatives when appropriate. Never send or publish; only draft for review.

items.name: Writing Desk
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Keeps a record of everything you have put out and writes the next one from what your business actually did, checking every draft against the archive so you never say the same thing twice. It writes; putting it out stays yours.
items.long_description:
Anybody who has promised themselves a weekly post knows the two ways it dies. The first is the blank page on the morning it is due. The second is quieter: three years in, nobody remembers what has already been covered, so the same piece gets written again with a different title and the readers notice before the writer does.

This keeps both from happening. It holds a record of everything you have published, and it reads that record before it writes a word, so a subject that has been covered comes back as “you wrote this in March, here is a different angle” rather than as a repeat.

And it writes from what your business actually did, not from a prompt. What your customers have been asking in your mail, what was said on your recorded calls, what you shipped or fixed or changed, and whatever material you have uploaded. Ask what you should write about and you get a subject with a reason attached.

It fits what it writes to where it is going: a blog post, release notes, a letter to customers, an update to members, each with its own readers, length and sound, kept as a row you can edit.

Nothing it writes is published. No tool here reaches a website or a mailing platform, so it hands you the finished piece and you put it out. Tell it you did and the archive stays true.

items.name: YNAB Keeper
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Reads your real YNAB. What you spent on a category this month, which transactions are still uncategorized, and where you have gone over. It can file the uncategorized ones with your say-so.
items.long_description:
The part of budgeting that nobody keeps up is the categorizing. Transactions land all week, most of them obvious, and the pile waits until the evening you finally sit down and click through forty of them deciding that yes, the corner shop was groceries.

Connect YNAB and your agent does the reading. Ask what is uncategorized and it lists them with payee and amount. Ask what you spent on a category this month and it answers from the real numbers. Ask where you are over and it compares budgeted against activity, category by category.

Tell it to file them and it proposes a category for each one, all at once, and shows you the list before anything moves. You are approving a page instead of clicking through forty screens.
setup_steps: Make the token in YNAB, under Account Settings, Developer Settings, New Token. It is one screen and there is nothing to configure beyond copying it.

items.name: Zotero Keeper
items.author: Otian AI
items.description: Reads your real Zotero library. Ask what you have on a subject and it searches your own references, and hands back the citation in the style you asked for.
items.long_description:
A reference library is a promise to your future self that you will be able to find the paper again. The promise breaks quietly: five hundred items in, the tags have drifted, half of them were saved from a browser button with whatever title the page had, and finding the one you half remember takes longer than searching the internet did.

Connect Zotero and your agent reads the real library. Ask what you have on a subject and it searches titles, creators and the full text of what is stored, and tells you what is there and where each one sits. Ask for the citation and it asks Zotero to format it, in the style you name, rather than assembling one itself and getting an initial wrong.

It reads what you have already collected. There is nothing to import and nothing to re-tag.
setup_steps: Make the key at zotero.org/settings/keys/new. Tick the read-only box unless you want your agent to be able to add references, and note the user id shown on that page: it is a number, not your username, and your agent needs it for every call.
